TL;DR


Our partner VIDRAFT released POCKET-27B-Pi, a coding agent packaged as one 16,547,400,320 byte GGUF (Q4_K_M, 16.5 GB). On the partner's own Terminal-Bench 2.1 run under the pi agent, it solved 28 of 48 shared tasks (58.3%), against 19 of 48 (39.6%) for the original Qwen3.8-27B. articles.title: Gemini 4 Neon Price: Cheaper Than Carbon After Dec 1?
articles.summary:
I spent this week pricing out Google's new Gemini 4 Neon for the kind of agent workloads I run, and the honest answer to "is it cheaper?" is: not today, yes from December 1. That flip catches a lot of teams off guard, so here is the math, the API changes that break old code, and when I would actually pick Neon.

articles.title: 6 Delphi behaviors that silently break when an AI ports your code to C#, Java or C++
articles.summary:
AI agents are good at producing code that compiles. With Delphi, "compiles" and "behaves the same" are far apart. Here are six behaviors I keep seeing agents get wrong — each one is measured on the Delphi 13 compiler, not recalled from memory.


  
  
  1. Round is banker's rounding


Round(2.5) = 2 and Round(3.5) = 4 in Delphi: halfway cases go to the nearest even number. C#'s Math.Round does the same by default, but Java's Math.round(2.5) and C++'s std::round(2.5) return 3. A port to Java or C++ that maps Round to the "obvious" function changes every halfway result.

articles.title: How do you robustly test a dynamically updated virtualized data grid with Playwright?
articles.summary:
🔥 Playwright Nightmare Scenario:
Your E2E tests are constantly flaking when interacting with data grids. Why? Virtualization!

📌 Problem Statement
Virtualized data grids (like those built with react-window or react-virtualized) are performance powerhouses. However, they only render a subset of items visible in the viewport.
❌  Elements you need to test aren't in the DOM until scrolled into view.
❌  Locators break as indices shift or elements are reused dynamically.
❌  Asynchronous data updates lead to unpredictable test failures.

articles.title: Censored vs. Truncated Regression in Python, Explained
articles.summary:
A simulated salary survey shows OLS shrinking a $5k-per-year effect to $3.2k, then recovers it with Tobit and truncated likelihoods built from scratch.
The post Censored vs. Truncated Regression in Python, Explained appeared first on Towards Data Science.

articles.title: AWS Releases a Free Local Emulator of AWS Built Entirely by Agents
articles.summary: AWS has released AWS Emulator, a free, CC0-licensed local stand-in for more than 200 of its services, generated from its public API models and aimed at the test loops of coding agents. AWS says agents wrote and maintain all of the code and publishes per-release fidelity scores. The docs say it does not evaluate IAM, and practitioners are split on trusting an emulator nobody reviewed. By Steef-Jan Wiggers
